To: Allyson Byrne <allyson@brightlane.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Release permissions & evidence checklist

Hi Allyson, Kim, Marissa —

Quick note to kick off the publicity & confidentiality coordination for BL-4829 before we finalize the order form. Two asks: 1) confirm whether BrightLane intends to publish a joint press release or merely permit a case study/reference; 2) provide the list of logo files and any constraints (square/horizontal, color restrictions, embargo windows).

Attached: BrightLane_OrderForm_v3.pdf (order form with proposed Publicity/Reference paragraph) and a redline of our standard MSA publicity clause (redlines_BrightLane_MSA.docx).

What we need from BrightLane by EOD Monday:
- Preferred announcement date (if any) or an embargo window
- Preferred logo variant(s) and attribution text
- Any additional confidentiality carveouts (e.g., redacted metrics)

Kim — can you flag anything in the MSA redline that will be a roadblock for Sales? Marissa — can you advise on a lightweight evidence ask (e.g., short quote + one logo) we can require in the order form to close? Naomi — FYI on customer marketing approvals.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightLane_OrderForm_v3.pdf (order form, 8 pages), redlines_BrightLane_MSA.docx (publicity clause redline)

From: Allyson Byrne <allyson@brightlane.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Release permissions & evidence checklist

Thanks, Priyom — appreciate the clear asks. Short answers for now while I pull assets:

- Announcement: We plan a soft case-study publish (blog + customer quote). No press release with reporters planned.
- Embargo: none; however, we prefer a coordinated publish window (we publish the case study on our site same day).
- Logos: I will upload three approved variants (color horizontal, mono square, and an html <svg> icon).
- Quote: we can provide a 2–3 sentence customer quote; may need a minor legal review.
- Confidentiality: We cannot disclose ARR numbers — redaction needed for any revenue references.

I see the MSA redline you sent. Our in-house counsel flagged the publicity clause for one item: they want a mandatory 10-business-day review period for any proposed customer quote. I'll send the formal redline later today.

—Allyson
Head of Marketing, BrightLane Analytics

Attachments: (will upload logo pack and redline by EOD)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Allyson Byrne <allyson@brightlane.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Release permissions & evidence checklist

Thanks Allyson — that approach (case study + coordinated publish) is straightforward and fits our typical ask. A couple of legal notes on the MSA redline I reviewed this morning:

1) 10-business-day mandatory review for customer quotes: acceptable, but we should convert to a "reasonable review period not to exceed 10 business days" to avoid an absolute veto.
2) Embargo / announcement coordination: add a mutual-notice clause that requires the parties to give 5 business days notice before public use of logos or case study materials (reasonable for ops).
3) Confidentiality carveout for revenue references: propose language allowing "non-specific performance metrics" instead of exact ARR (e.g., percent improvement or high-level descriptors).

I edited redlines_BrightLane_MSA.docx and tracked comments. Please confirm if BrightLane counsel is willing to accept the softened review language and the 5-day notice. If they insist on an absolute 10-business-day approval window or continued redaction of any metric beyond the agreed high-level descriptors, we should loop in Legal for escalated concession approval.

Marissa — for Sales ops: if BrightLane will supply one logo + one approved quote within the order execution window, that's enough for our case-study process. If they want to delay quote approval beyond 10 business days, we should mark the evidence requirement optional and allow a use-for-reference-only clause.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Kimberly — thanks for the suggested language. Our counsel accepted the mutual-notice and the 5-day coordination, but they are firm on the 10-business-day review for customer quotes (their reasoning: internal approval cycles across product/strategy). They asked if Redwood can add a fallback: if we don't respond after 10 business days, the quote is considered approved. That would avoid indefinite holds.

Also: our legal team proposes a specific redaction sentence for revenue references: "Parties agree that any revenue figures will be redacted; public materials may reference anonymized or percentage-based improvements with mutually agreed language."

I'll attach our formal redline (redlines_BrightLane_MSA_BLR.docx) in the Hub folder and shared the preliminary logo pack (BrightLane_logos_v1.zip). Can Redwood accept the auto-approval after 10 business days as a compromise?

—Allyson

Attachments: BrightLane_logos_v1.zip (3 files: horizontal_color.svg, mono_square.png, icon.svg), redlines_BrightLane_MSA_BLR.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -07:00

All — quick operational decision to keep the deal moving: Sales is fine with the 10-business-day auto-approval fallback, provided we add two safeguards in the order form: 1) a limited 30‑day window post-execution for quote collection (we won't keep the deliverable open indefinitely), and 2) a requirement that any public materials include the agreed redaction language for revenue references.

I'll update BrightLane_OrderForm_v3.pdf to include a short checkbox flow: "Customer provides logo + 2-3 sentence quote within 30 days. If no response within 10 business days after Redwood submits proposed quote, quote is auto-approved for publication subject to agreed redactions."

Kim — if Legal is comfortable with those two guardrails, I can send the updated order form and we can move to signature. Naomi — can you schedule a single cross-team sync with Marketing to align on publication timing after signature?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Partnerships Ops
Redwood Inference
